title: Inclusion of Tripartite Standard for Contracting with Self-Employed Persons in Reporting by SGX-listed Firms
what_it_is: Inclusion of Tripartite Standard for Contracting with Self-Employed Persons in Reporting by SGX-listed Firms

sections.label: Tripartite Standards and ESG reporting
sections.summary: The Government was asked whether it will work with SGX to define Tripartite Standards as material ESG factors for listed firms' sustainability reporting.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean
sentences.text: asked the Prime Minister whether the Government will consider working with the Singapore Exchange (SGX) to define Tripartite Standards, such as the Tripartite Standard for Contracting with Self-Employed Persons, as a component of the material environmental, social and governance factors under SGX-listed firms' sustainability reporting.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: This also applies to reporting on environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Reporting requirements on such aspects are not overly prescriptive, as companies' business models, strategies and stakeholders vary widely.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Companies adopt the Tripartite Standards on a voluntary basis and have to assess which factors, including the Tripartite Standards, have a material impact on their business performance and prospects and, thus, should be disclosed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Companies also make employment-related disclosures on factors, such as occupational health and safety, diversity and inclusion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Manpower (MOM) and the Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP) continue to promote and encourage companies to adopt the Tripartite Standards.

sections.label: Voluntary Tripartite Standards adoption
sections.summary: SGX disclosure requirements promote information quality, not how companies are run, so Tripartite Standards are adopted voluntarily, with MOM and agencies encouraging adoption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: As I mentioned earlier on, SGX disclosure requirements are, in fact, intended to promote availability and the quality of information on the companies' performance, but not to prescribe how a company should actually be run, and that is why companies adopt these Tripartite Standards on a voluntary basis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: I think Ms Jean See also had a similar written question to MOM.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: That question also fleshed out how it is voluntary and how if a company has adopted the Tripartite Standards, there are certain benefits to it, including a Tripartite Standards logo, that will confer some form of additional reputational benefits to the company.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: But in the same way, for SGX-listed companies, companies may approach TAFEP to learn more about good employment standards and Tripartite Standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
sentences.text: I think MOM and other agencies are, in fact, promoting and encouraging companies, either listed or non-listed, to adopt these standards.
